agree.reason: The candid refusal to promise profit, the cost cut and the $250,000 already committed help, but a partner who thinks sales are too slow gets no target for spring sales and no monthly cash report, so they have little reason to change their view.

honest.reason: The update avoids the profit claim and is honest about the mite-treatment confound, but it adds an unsupported line that the company doesn't know whether it has lost deals, and "autumn 2027" is stated without showing how it was worked out.

works_the_facts.reason: The runway to March, the $35k monthly revenue and the post-bridge runway are worked out correctly, but there is no growth rate, no per-sensor margin ($17), no subscription revenue at scale, and no calculation of the revenue needed to break even at $75k a month.

right_comparison.reason: It shows the alternative clearly: without the bridge, cash runs out in March just as the selling season starts. But it doesn't compare the current pace of customer growth with the pace needed.

qualification.reason: The spring "real test" sets no customer or revenue threshold and says nothing about what happens if it is missed. The only dated, checkable commitment is the $75k cost cut by February.

objections.reason: It never says how fast sales need to grow or how the company will speed them up, which is the reader's actual worry, and it leaves out the monthly cash report that would reassure a cautious investor.

fit.reason: It is under 600 words and uses a sensible update format, but it leaves placeholders for the reply date (known to be December 1) and the sender's name, and never names HiveSense.
